data.narrative:
Hadrian, a Series D robotics and manufacturing company, was last valued at $1.6B post-money following $1.37B in total capital raised. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 4 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies, with a broader comp universe that includes 1 public company and 8 private peers.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using typical Series D to next-stage advancement mechanics, implies a 1.5x step-up to $2.4B on the $1.6B base. Peer-median analysis across Divergent ($2.3B Series E), Exotec ($2.0B Series D), Agile Robots ($1.0B Series C), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B Series C) yields a median of $1.5B, with a range of $1.0B to $2.3B. These methods reflect the company's positioning relative to growth-stage robotics players at comparable development stages.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $1.3B to $2.8B, with a median of $1.9B. The current $1.6B valuation sits at the lower end of this range, 15% below the median implied value. Key uncertainties include capital efficiency relative to peers, customer concentration, and near-term pathway to profitability or exit. The gap between stage-progression and peer-median methods ($900M spread) reflects variation in how comparable companies are valued at different funding stages.
